name: Czech
script: Latin with extra letters: á, č, ď, é, ě, í, ň, ó, ř, š, ť, ú, ů, ý, ž; left to right
basis: University beginner Czech courses: ČVUT Czech/Foreign Language 1 lesson list and Charles University summer school Beginners I (Léto s češtinou)
src: Czech Technical University (ČVUT), 'Czech/Foreign Language 1' syllabus on bilakniha.cvut.cz: ordered lessons (pronunciation, být / mít, gender, likes and family, adjectives, accusative and restaurant, locative and directions, shopping, Co chcete?), textbooks Communicative Czech elementary and Czech Step by Step 1

Charles University Faculty of Arts summer school, Czech for Beginners I course plan (PDF, textbook Léto s češtinou): lessons 1–6 with být, gender, accusative, mít, numbers, jít / jet, verb groups, possessives, future, chutná mi / líbí se mi, moct / muset / chtít
note: Both sources put být and mít first, the accusative (ordering food) before the locative (where things are, directions), and modal verbs and liking verbs in the middle; the order here follows them. The split of sounds into three lessons, the past-tense lesson (not in either source's beginner part) and the exact titles are common course practice and my own judgment.
hardest: ř, and long versus short vowels that change meaning (byt / být)
Seven cases; the accusative and locative already at A1, with endings by gender
Verb groups (-ám, -ím, -uju / -uji) and irregular verbs like jít, jet, moct, chtít
Numbers that change the noun: 1 koruna, 2 koruny, 5 korun

items: Alphabet and the háček letters: č, š, ž, ř, ě, ň, ď, ť
Long vowels (á, é, í, ó, ú / ů, ý) and stress on the first syllable
Hard sounds: ř, ch, and voiceless final consonants
Greetings: dobrý den, ahoj, na shledanou; vy and ty
být: jsem, jsi, je… and Co je to? Kdo je to?
Introducing yourself: Jmenuji se…, Jsem z…
mít and mít rád: have and like
Yes/no questions and ne-: nemám, nejsem
Adjectives: Jaký je? dobrý, dobrá, dobré
Accusative: Dám si kávu, Mám bratra
Ordering and paying: Kolik to stojí? koruna, koruny, korun
Family, jobs and possessives: můj, moje, tvůj
Liking food and things: chutná mi, líbí se mi
moct, muset, chtít: can, must, want
Time and days: Kolik je hodin? v pondělí
Going on foot and by transport: jít and jet
Directions: Jak se dostanu na…? rovně, doleva, doprava
Shopping and clothes: Co chcete? colours and sizes
Past tense: byl jsem, dělala jsem
